title: Sharp thresholds for graph properties
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proofs (2026) of the Friedgut-Kalai threshold conjectures: every nontrivial increasing graph property has threshold width at most 2^19 log(1/(2 eps)) / (log n)^2, and r-uniform hypergraph properties have width O_r((log n)^(-r/(r-1))). The first lesson develops biased Fourier analysis, the Margulis-Russo formula, a biased hypercontractive inequality with explicit constants and a low-degree estimate for functions with small individual influences. The second restricts to the edges meeting a random block of vertices, captures each Fourier support at one vertex, and proves the variance-influence bound and the threshold theorem for graphs. The third does the same for hypergraphs.
